proposition.subject: Energy logistics and refining bottlenecks keep fuel costs high despite export recovery
proposition.body: Our 6 October scan identified a durable energy-logistics and refining bottleneck as confirmed. What stood out was that despite Middle East crude exports recovering to pre-war levels, fuel delivery costs remain elevated due to tanker risks, insurance, refinery damage, and inventory depletion. We are developing an evidence-backed contribution around how refinery damage, medium-sour processing limits, and reduced inventories interrupt the conversion of crude into usable fuel — while keeping unresolved the duration of tanker risks, refinery restoration schedules, fuel price pass-through, and inventory accessibility. Would this be suitable as an article or research contribution for Oil & Gas Journal? If useful, I can send a concise finished draft with sources for review.

proposition.subject: Energy logistics bottleneck deepens despite crude export recovery
proposition.body: Our 6 October scan identified a durable energy-logistics and refining bottleneck as CONFIRMED. What stood out was that longer routes and ship-to-ship transfers continue impacting operational tanker availability distinctly from crude production. We are developing an evidence-backed contribution around this maritime logistics angle — while keeping unresolved issues such as the duration of tanker risk, refinery restoration schedules, fuel price pass-through, and accessible inventory quality explicit. Would this be suitable as an article or research contribution for Riviera Maritime Media / Tanker Shipping & Trade? If useful, I can send a concise finished draft with sources for review.

proposition.subject: Middle East crude export recovery reveals tanker and refining bottlenecks
proposition.body: Our 6 October scan identified a durable energy-logistics and refining bottleneck is supporting high delivered fuel costs even when crude export volumes improve. What stood out was safe tanker capacity and war-risk insurance distinguish recovered crude flows from delivered fuel availability. We are developing an evidence-backed contribution around how repeated tanker attacks, prolonged routes, damaged refineries, and depleted inventories elevate freight and fuel prices — while keeping unresolved issues such as tanker risk duration, refinery repair schedules, fuel pass-through, and accessible inventory location explicit. Would this be suitable as an article or research contribution for TradeWinds? If useful, I can send a concise finished draft with sources for review.
